# hubspot_report (Data Source)

Looks up one HubSpot report by `id` or exact `name`, exposing its metadata, permissions, tags and a `raw_json` snapshot. Name lookups search with HubSpot's contains-match `q` filter and then keep only exact, case-sensitive name matches; the report is then always fetched by ID, so the result (including `raw_json`) is identical whichever way it was looked up. To find the reports on a dashboard, use `hubspot_reports` with `dashboard_id` or the `report_ids` of `hubspot_dashboard`.

`raw_json` holds the API object canonicalized — sorted keys, 2-space indent, trailing newline — with the volatile view-tracking fields (`lastViewedAt`, `lastViewedByUserId`) stripped. It is meant for **committed snapshots** (write it with `local_file` and check it into git): a snapshot only diffs on real changes, and fields HubSpot adds to the API later are captured without a provider release. The typed `last_viewed_at` / `last_viewed_by_user_id` attributes still expose the view-tracking values.

**Report configuration (query, data sources, filters, visualization) is not exposed by the HubSpot API at all** — not even readable — so it cannot be captured here; only metadata, permissions, tags and dashboard layout are. Exporting report data (the API's emailed CSV/PDF export) is intentionally not offered: it is a side-effecting action on CRM record data, outside this provider's configuration-plane scope.

**The Analytics Reporting API is a public beta** (`/analytics/reporting/2027-03-beta`), so this is beta-backed per the provider's [API stability policy](https://github.com/revosai/terraform-provider-hubspot/blob/main/ROADMAP.md#api-stability-policy). The portal must opt into the beta (via the associated product update in HubSpot) and the token needs the `reporting.full.read` scope (plus `reporting.full.write` to create, clone or archive).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Look up a report by its exact (case-sensitive) name. Errors when no report,
# or more than one, has that name.
data "hubspot_report" "revenue" {
  name = "Revenue by rep"
}

# ...or by ID, including an archived report.
data "hubspot_report" "legacy" {
  id       = "987654"
  archived = true
}

# Report IDs are what dashboards reference and what hubspot_report clones from.
output "revenue_report_id" {
  value = data.hubspot_report.revenue.id
}

# Metadata snapshot (permissions, tags, owner, ...) for committing to git.
# Report configuration (query/visualization) is not exposed by the HubSpot API.
resource "local_file" "revenue_report_snapshot" {
  filename = "${path.module}/reporting/reports/${data.hubspot_report.revenue.id}.json"
  content  = data.hubspot_report.revenue.raw_json
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `archived` (Boolean) Set to `true` to look up an **archived** report instead of an active one (HubSpot keeps the two apart: an archived report is not found without it, and an active one is not found with it). Defaults to `false`.
- `id` (String) The report's ID. Exactly one of `id` or `name` must be set.
- `name` (String) The report's exact name (case-sensitive). Exactly one of `id` or `name` must be set; a name lookup errors when no report, or more than one, has that name.

### Read-Only

- `archived_at` (String) When the report was archived (ISO 8601); null for an active report.
- `business_unit_id` (String) Business unit (brand) the report belongs to; `0` is the default business unit.
- `created_at` (String) When the report was created (ISO 8601).
- `created_by_user_id` (String) HubSpot user ID of the report's creator.
- `description` (String) The report's description (null when unset).
- `last_viewed_at` (String) When the report was last viewed (ISO 8601). Volatile — it changes whenever anyone opens the report — so it is excluded from `raw_json`.
- `last_viewed_by_user_id` (String) HubSpot user ID of the last viewer. Volatile; excluded from `raw_json`.
- `owner_user_id` (String) HubSpot user ID of the report's owner.
- `permissions` (Attributes) Who can access the report. `type` is one of `PRIVATE`, `EVERYONE_VIEW`, `EVERYONE_EDIT` or `SPECIFIC`; with `SPECIFIC`, list the users/teams in `view` and/or `edit`. Grants are sets (order-insensitive) and are only allowed with `SPECIFIC`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--permissions))
- `raw_json` (String) The full API report object as canonical JSON for committed snapshots: sorted keys, 2-space indent, trailing newline, view-tracking fields (`lastViewedAt`, `lastViewedByUserId`) stripped.
- `tags` (Attributes List) Tags on the report (read-only: the API cannot set tags). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tags))
- `updated_at` (String) When the report was last updated (ISO 8601).
- `updated_by_user_id` (String) HubSpot user ID of the user who last updated the report.

<a id="nestedatt--permissions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `permissions`

Read-Only:

- `edit` (Attributes Set) Users/teams granted edit access to the report (`SPECIFIC` only). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--permissions--edit))
- `type` (String) Permission type.
- `view` (Attributes Set) Users/teams granted view access to the report (`SPECIFIC` only). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--permissions--view))

<a id="nestedatt--permissions--edit"></a>
### Nested Schema for `permissions.edit`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) HubSpot user ID or team ID.
- `type` (String) Grantee kind: `USER` or `TEAM`.


<a id="nestedatt--permissions--view"></a>
### Nested Schema for `permissions.view`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) HubSpot user ID or team ID.
- `type` (String) Grantee kind: `USER` or `TEAM`.



<a id="nestedatt--tags"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tags`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) Tag ID.
- `name` (String) Tag name.
